pages.content:
If you’re new here, welcome.
I’m glad you found this place.

FIRST BLOG

Cell to Self is not a comeback story. It’s real life after prison, written in real time. There’s no polish, no pretending, and no neatly wrapped ending. Just the messy work of becoming yourself again.

You won’t find a single, complete explanation of my past here. Instead, you’ll find pieces of it — moments, memories, letters, poems, and reflections — shared as they surface and make sense. This space isn’t about rewriting history. It’s about telling the truth as it unfolds.

How this space works

I write in a few different ways, depending on where I’m at that day.

Dear Prison Pals
Letters I’d send anyway.
These are letters and updates I send to friends still in prison — honest, sometimes funny, sometimes heavy, always real.

Ink on the Inside
Poems written when words were the only way out.
These poems were written in prison, without knowing who would ever read them. They aren’t polished for performance. They’re preserved as they were.

After the Headline
Writing away imposter syndrome.
This is where I write about identity, work, fear, and living under a story I didn’t get to tell, while choosing to become more than what people think they know.

Healing in Real Time
Working through what still hurts.

This is where I write about healing as it unfolds. Untangling trauma, working the steps, learning to forgive, and letting go in real time.

You don’t have to read everything in order. You don’t have to agree with me. You just have to be willing to read honestly.

This isn’t a blueprint. It’s just my story unfolding in honesty, humor, and hope.

Still not sure where to start?

pages.content:
About Cell to Self

I’ve only been out of prison for a month; I didn’t come out magically put together.
I came out confused, grateful, overwhelmed, and trying to figure out how to use a debit card without panicking.

Cell to Self is where I write through that in real time.

This isn’t a before-and-after story. It’s a during.
It’s what happens when you’re free, still scared, still laughing, still learning how to live in your own skin again… and you decide to tell the truth about it.

Sometimes that truth is deep.
Sometimes it’s ridiculous.
Often, it’s both.

FIRST BLOG POST

What This Space Is

Cell to Self is a blog about reentry, recovery, faith, motherhood, and starting over, told without polish and without pretending I’ve figured it all out.

I write about what it’s actually like to come home after prison: the big things, like addiction, recovery, rebuilding relationships, and learning how to live differently this time. I also write about the small things no one prepares you for, the culture shock, the fear, the humor, the quiet messiness of becoming someone new, and the moments that catch you off guard when you least expect them.

Some days this space is reflective.
Some days it’s light.
Most days, it’s just messy.

If you’re looking for a blueprint, this isn’t it.
If you’re looking for honesty, humor, and a little hope hiding in real life, you’re in the right place.

Why I Write This Way

For a long time, my life was reduced to headlines, case numbers, and assumptions. Writing gave me something back: my voice.

I wrote in prison.
I write now.
I write because it helps me make sense of where I’ve been and where I’m going.

This is me healing in real time, on the page, out loud, and sometimes mid-mess. It’s a journey certain to be chaotic, sometimes ridiculous, and unfinished, but I am praying it also leads to healing and hope for both of us!

This blog isn’t about erasing the past.
It’s about rewriting the story from here, with footnotes, crossed-out sentences, and chapters I never thought I’d get to write.

Who This Is For

This space is for anyone who’s made mistakes, been misunderstood, or maybe even felt like the world would be better off without them. It’s for anyone who’s had their story told for them, and wants to take it back.

Whether you’re coming home and trying to find your footing, in recovery and still feeling a little lost, or simply loving someone in either of these places, I hope something here meets you where you are.

You don’t have to be ready to heal.
You don’t have to be optimistic.
You don’t even have to know what you believe yet.

You just have to be willing to come along for the ride.

A Note on Faith

Faith is part of my life, not as a slogan or a checklist, but as something that shows up quietly along the way.

It’s there in the moments that feel steady and the ones that don’t. It shows up in second chances, unexpected grace, the people who appear when I don’t think I deserve it, and the reminders that I’m not doing this alone.

I don’t write to convince anyone of what to believe. I write from my heart, honestly, imperfectly, and with room for questions.

Take what resonates.
Leave what doesn’t.

I’ll be here, writing it as it unfolds.

If you’re not sure where to start, this is my very first post in the form of the letter I wrote my prison pals when I first got out of prison.

posts.title: Nothing Exciting to Report
posts.excerpt: Sometimes I don’t have some huge adventure or crazy story to tell y’all. Sometimes life is just peaceful, quiet, and normal. I think that’s kind of beautiful.
posts.content:
Sometimes I love the fact that my life goes weeks being so peaceful and quiet that I don’t have anything exciting to tell y’all. I’m almost done with my bedroom and will send a picture next time. I have a headboard to put together first. Wish me luck!

I do have exciting news now though. I’M GETTING A DOG FROM A LOCAL SHELTER!!! She is under 25 pounds and over 6 months old, just like my apartment requires. And she’s already potty trained. Thank God! I’ll send y’all a picture when I get her home.

Somehow I always manage to come into some kind of boy drama, but these days I just be walking away like it’s nothing. Oh? Red flag? Gotta bounce. Like my old superintendent used to say, I’m just out here breaking all the hearts. Really though, I just want a strong Christian man who will pray with me and bring consistency and stability into my life. Is that really too much to ask?

My 18-year-old son, the one I gave the car to, is in Marine boot camp right now. I still haven’t gotten to talk to him myself, but I get updates, and he graduates in a week! I’m so freaking proud of him. My 22-year-old is still struggling some. She and her partner are moving in with someone else where they’ll have their own space, so I’m praying this will be a better situation for them.

My 15-year-old, Khloe, is still planning to go into ministry. I sent my sister money for her learner’s permit. And my 10-year-old, Kasey, had a friend invite him on a pirate cruise, so I got to pay for him to go. I am grateful that even though I don’t get to be part of their everyday lives right now, I get updates and I can still help them experience life in little ways. Those little ways mean more to me than I can explain.

Also, if y’all need me to look up anything like careers, halfway houses, reentry resources, whatever, please ask me. I will do it. Sometimes it takes me a little time, but I’ve already been doing it for some of you, and I genuinely love doing it. It’s become one of my passions.

I can help with resumes, reentry goals, career plans, halfway houses, or just figuring out what steps you can start taking now to set yourself up for success when you come home. And I don’t care if your release date feels forever away. Start anyway. You don’t have to wait until you’re 10 years or six months from the gate to start building the life you want to walk into.

I signed the paperwork to transfer my probation out of state. The president of my company, our chief administrative officer, and my direct supervisor all wrote letters to probation supporting my transfer. I am so lucky to have a career with a company that is so encouraging and supportive of me. They know where I’ve been, they love me right where I am, and they cheer me on for where I am going. I don’t know if I will ever get used to having people believe in me like that. So cool.

Sometimes I still have moments where I look around at this quiet little life I’m building and think about how scared I was to come home. And now my biggest problems are putting together a headboard, deciding what to name my dog, and dodging red flags.

I’ll take it.

Y’all, God is so freaking good.

XOXO

posts.title: Sometimes Home Was Hayley
posts.excerpt: Hayley is gone. This is her story. Her story with me, for the short time I was blessed to call her mine. I often have to remind myself that she’s gone. I still reach for my phone to text or call her several times a day. She’s been gone for two months now, and somehow […]
posts.content:
Hayley is gone.

This is her story. Her story with me, for the short time I was blessed to call her mine.

I often have to remind myself that she’s gone. I still reach for my phone to text or call her several times a day. She’s been gone for two months now, and somehow it still doesn’t feel real. My life just doesn’t feel right without her.

She wasn’t okay, so maybe I have to be okay for her now.

Hayley and I were supposed to be roommates at the Oxford House when I first got out of prison, but she was still struggling with her alcoholism. She went to detox the night before I got out, so we saved a bed for her in a different room.

Hayley was a fighter. She was strong.

Her sobriety date ended up being just three days after my prison release date. So every month, we celebrated together. Another month sober for her. Another month free for me. We counted days together.

I remember meeting her, but honestly, I didn’t pay too much attention to her at first. I had my first new friend out of prison over at the house, and at that point I was still mainly focused on myself. It took me time to let people in. Somewhere along the way, Hayley started giving her roommate and me rides to meetings.

And Hayley grew on me quickly. Somehow, she just infiltrated her way into my life.

Her smile was contagious, and she had this fake little laugh-giggle she’d do after saying something funny that reminded me of my cousin. There was something about her I admired almost immediately. Hayley had this beauty, passion, and grace that seemed to flow out of her naturally. Kindness and compassion came easily to her. She could meet someone and almost immediately see the person underneath whatever mess they were carrying.

Me? I was a walking contradiction. Grace was something I had to work for.

But prison had given me some things Hayley needed too. I had stopped caring so much about what other people thought of me. I had learned to set boundaries—and actually stick to them—more than I ever had before. I had also learned that I could love someone for whatever good I saw inside them without allowing them unlimited access to my life. Sometimes loving someone meant walking away. Sometimes it meant loving them from a distance.

And prison had taught me how to let shit go. After years of having absolutely no control over my own life, I had finally learned to stop trying to control everything else. I learned how to go with the flow.

Hayley had some things I needed. And somehow, I had some things she needed too.

Somewhere in the middle of what she had and what I had, we found each other.

And that was it.

Hayley and I bonded at a soul-deep level.

She began teaching me what true friendship looked like.

She became my Hayley, and I was even introduced as Hayley’s Amy if she wasn’t there. Lol. 

I unexpectedly got laid off from the ministry that had hired me a year before I got out of prison. Then I got an amazing temporary job offer. There was just one problem: it was across town, and I didn’t have a car.

I spent hours calculating my income and my options. Eventually, I decided that even if I had to spend $250 a week on Lyft, the experience and pay would be worth it. I could still pay my bills and very slowly save for a car.

Hayley was about to start a new job off the highway. She insisted it wouldn’t be out of her way to take me and told me to just cover half the gas we used every day. It was kinda on her way, but I was working ten- and eleven-hour days while she worked eight. She could have slept in or gone to her home group at 6 a.m. every morning, but Hayley wouldn’t take no for an answer.

She had an answer for every objection I gave her. It gave her time to do her morning readings. She could meditate before work. While she waited for me in the afternoon, she could run her errands. It was perfect, she told me.

I knew damn well it wasn’t perfect. I knew this arrangement was a whole lot more convenient for me than it was for her. But eventually, I understood something: she wasn’t offering because it was convenient. She was offering because she loved me.

Apparently, Hayley was going to help me whether I liked it or not.

I didn’t understand why someone would do all of that for me yet, but I began thanking God for putting Hayley in my life. Every day, I thanked God for this amazing woman.

And so it began. Hayley got me to work on time every single day. In the evenings, I never had to wait for my ride. She was always waiting for me. It was actually a while before anyone at work even realized I didn’t have a car.

We went to our favorite meetings after work. Then, when my roommate moved out, Hayley moved in. It made sense because we were basically already living on the same schedule anyway. She’d also been having trouble sleeping because her old roommate kept completely different hours than we did.

She worried about some of my choices in men, and honestly, I worried about some of hers too. But no matter what happened, Hayley loved me unconditionally. She would drop anything at the drop of a hat to be there for me.

There was really only one person who ever came before me: her beautiful, talented daughter, Grayson. Grayson was her everything. I’m so grateful I got to meet G before Hayley left us.

I worried about Hayley too. I worried about her being stuck on her Fourth Step and about some of the resentments she was still carrying. But she always promised me she was alright, and most of the time, she seemed happy.

Meanwhile, my own life was changing unbelievably fast. After only a month of working, I had saved half of what I needed to purchase a car I’d found. I also had enough to pay $500 in child support and set up the payment plan I needed to get my driver’s license back.

I put the down payment on the car, and by the beginning of February, it was paid off.

Less than three months out of prison, I had a car.

I had worked my ass off for it, but I also knew something else. Before I could drive myself forward, Hayley had helped carry me there.

By this time, my boss and I had become close friends too. I’d finally told him my entire sordid past, and I had started taking him up on some of the rides he’d been offering me. Pretty soon, he and Hayley were actually arguing over who was taking me where.

Seriously. How could someone in my position be so lucky?

When Hayley drove me to pick up my car, she was sad-happy. She was so proud of me, but she told the man I bought it from that she was sad too because now she was going to lose so much of her time with me.

My heart was full.

When someone tried to tell my story to my new employer before I was ready, Hayley was right there. She held my hand, ready to catch me if I fell and cheering me on when I didn’t know what was going to happen next.

I think Hayley loved me before I truly knew how to love myself.

She always answered the phone. She always had good advice. And when I thought my entire life was falling apart, somehow Hayley would be there with a peanut butter Snickers and a Dr Pepper—two of my favorite comfort items. Her way of saying, I’ve got you.

Around Christmas, I went with her to give Grayson her presents. One of them was a 3D printer, and Grayson went crazy over it. A few days later, Hayley came home with these little boats, blue blended into green. Grayson had made three matching ones: one for herself, one for her mom, and one for me. Mine still sits on my nightstand.

Then I fell for the wrong guy.

Hayley was terrified for me. She saw me beginning to lose myself long before I could see it. She fought for me, and for a while, I fell away.

There’s a much longer story behind that, and maybe I’ll tell it someday. I was “falling in love” and rushing around. I was spending less and less time at home and more and more time with this guy. Hayley and he would argue over who got what days, and honestly, it made me feel special and loved.

I was still hitting my meetings and working seven days a week. I had three nights with him and four with Hayley. Saturday nights with Hayley were supposed to be the most important part of my week: church, dinner, meeting. That routine had become part of my foundation of stability and balance.

Then one Saturday, everything got messy.

There was an incident at the house involving medication I mistakenly thought was mine. The house believed I may have taken it intentionally. I didn’t show up to the house meeting the following day to defend myself, and they unanimously voted to ask me to leave.

At the time, I didn’t care—or at least I told myself I didn’t. The atmosphere in the house had already been terrible, and instead of going to that house meeting, I let the guy I was seeing take me to get my hair done.

But when I heard the vote had been unanimous, I’ll admit it hurt.

Now, with distance, I understand why Hayley voted the way she did.

Back then, I didn’t.

And the man I was with knew exactly where to push.

He played the idea that Hayley wasn’t my true friend if she could vote against me over and over and over in my head until eventually, I started believing it.

Once again, I allowed a man to convince me that one of the people who loved me most wasn’t really my friend.

And that’s when I fell away. But she waited.

Hayley didn’t stop loving me because I got lost for a while. When I finally needed somewhere to fall, her arms were still open.

That’s who Hayley was.

She was the only person to call me by my prison nickname, “I Am Amy.” LOL. Nobody else outside of prison understood it. Just Hayley did.

She was also the only person who truly understood some of the trauma I dealt with during those first few months at my new job.

I hope she can see me now.

I still struggle, but I’m so much stronger when it comes to men and keeping myself first. I’m learning that love isn’t supposed to require me to disappear. Hayley saw how badly I needed to learn that long before I did.

At some point, I texted Hayley and asked if I could use her real name in my blog. I explained that I rarely used anyone’s real name in my writing. The only time I did was when someone was such an important part of my story that I knew they were a permanent part of it.

She told me she would be honored.

So I used her name.

I wrote:

Sometimes home is Hayley waiting at a meeting with a peanut butter Snickers and a Dr Pepper.

I had no idea how much those words would eventually mean.

Toward the end of my story with Hayley, she was struggling more and more. There were nights when she felt like she couldn’t do life anymore, and I was the only one she was willing to talk to.

I felt honored that she trusted me.

I was also terrified.

Many nights, I sat on the phone with her for hours just reminding her I was there and I loved her. I would coax her to go to sleep or ask her to let me come over. Sometimes she seemed okay the next morning. Sometimes it took longer.

I felt helpless. I didn’t know how to fix what was hurting inside my friend, so I prayed. I prayed that whenever she didn’t know what to do anymore, she would keep calling me.

One morning, after a particularly rough night, I texted her and asked if there was anything in the entire world I could do to make her feel even a little better.

She said teleporting her and Grayson to a secluded island.

Okay.

Slight problem.

I hadn’t quite figured out teleportation yet.

I thought and thought about what I could possibly do. Finally, I decided the next best option was obviously a genie lamp. You gotta love Amazon Prime. It showed up the next day. It didn’t actually work, but I hope it made her smile.

Not long after that, Hayley went to visit family. As soon as she got back, I texted her that I missed her. She replied right back.

I was getting ready to leave Florida for work, and originally, I’d created a Facebook event inviting everyone to come say goodbye. By Tuesday morning, I deleted it. I realized I didn’t really care that much about saying goodbye to a huge group of people. I just wanted Hayley. 

My sister and I already had dinner planned for Friday, so after work Tuesday, I called Hayley. I wanted to ask her to have dinner with just me and her on Thursday.

She didn’t answer. That wasn’t like Hayley. Hayley always answered.

I tried again. Straight to voicemail now.

I started to panic and texted her to call me back ASAP. This was a woman who would answer my phone call while she was on a date with the new boyfriend she was head over heels for. Something wasn’t right.

Then I saw her Facebook post from the beach. She wrote about being excited to start a new chapter.

To someone looking from the outside, it probably sounded beautiful. But I wasn’t on the outside. I was on the inside Hayley. Something about it didn’t feel right.

I called and texted again and again throughout the night.

I didn’t know until the next morning that while I was desperately trying to reach her, Hayley was already slipping away from us on that beach.

There are some moments your life divides itself around.

Before and after.

This was one of mine.

I don’t know everything that happened inside Hayley that day. I don’t know why that particular day became the day when the pain felt bigger than the possibilities.

I wish I did.

God, I wish I did.

One of the things that brings me comfort is knowing that during our time together, Hayley and I grew in our faith together through church, prayer, the Bible, recovery, and love. I had nudged her back toward God at times, and she had certainly nudged me toward Him too.

There are so many things Hayley won’t get to see.

She won’t see Grayson finish high school. She won’t see her graduate college or get married. She won’t see the life I kept telling her I was going to build come to fruition. And she won’t get to see me becoming the woman she seemed to believe I could be long before I did.

After I got the news, I picked up the little blue-and-green boat Grayson made for us. For almost 24 hours, I didn’t put it down. I held it. I slept with it. I cried with it. I screamed with it. I prayed with it.

I don’t even completely understand why. It was just the only thing that made me feel close to her and brought me the slightest bit of comfort.

That day, I only talked to my sponsor. I didn’t try to make myself okay. I didn’t try to find some profound lesson in it. I just let myself feel everything.

Before I left Florida, I went to the beach where Hayley died. I needed to say goodbye.

I cried and talked to her. I walked along the beach and picked up shells that reminded me of her. I drew a heart in the sand and told her what I was doing and where I was going. 

She took a piece of my heart with her on that beach that day. And I carried a piece of hers with me to the next state.

Sometimes home really is a person. Hayley was mine.

So yes, two months later, I still reach for my phone to call her. Two months later, something happens and she’s still the only person I desperately want to tell. Two months later, there are moments when I need to hear her voice so badly that I cry.

But two months later, I’m also a little more okay every day.

Not because I’m leaving Hayley behind.

Because I’m learning how to carry her with me.

She wasn’t okay.

But I will be.

For her. And for me.

I love you, Hayley.

This is your story.
This is our story.
This is my healing.
And this is my goodbye.

posts.title: Hey! That’s Mine!
posts.excerpt: After years of having no control over where I lived or where I slept, I finally have a place that’s all mine. My bedroom. My kitchen. My shower. I even named the Wi-Fi “Mine.” 😂
posts.content:
Hiiiiiii!!!!!!

Some of y’all need to get better about writing me back. 😂 By the way, how long do I have to wait before I can visit?

I got to move into my apartment by the job site I’m working at in Arkansas early, and I am SO happy here.

I just feel this new sense of freedom there that I didn’t feel in FL. I was doing amazing here, but now I truly feel free.

I say here because I’m actually home in FL for almost a week to renew my travel pass. I still have my place here too. He does Airbnb and just blocks off the days I come home, so I still have my room when I’m back.

But y’all…

The gratitude I feel waking up in a place that is all mine is probably indescribable to most people, but I know y’all will understand.

I can’t wait for you to feel it again too.

I literally walk around my apartment looking at everything and saying, “Mine.”

My bedroom. Mine.

My kitchen. Mine.

My shower. Mine.

I even named my Wi-Fi network “Mine.” LMAO.

After so many years of having absolutely no control over where I lived or even where I slept, I don’t think I’ll ever take something as simple as having my own front door for granted.

I love my job.

I love everyone I work with, and they seem to love me too. I didn’t even want to come back to FL because I have to miss work Monday and Tuesday, and I DON’T WANNA MISS. 😂

My job just officially got its first trucks of steel for the building, and it was such an adrenaline rush to be there at the very beginning and watch everything start ramping up.

Y’all know how much I LOVE coding, but I honestly think I should have gone into heavy equipment when I was in prison instead.

My job is literally to be in charge of ordering and managing all of the heavy equipment on-site.

We will be using boom lifts, forklifts up to 55K, and FOUR cranes—three lattice boom crawlers and one RT crane.

And I have been driving a buggy around the site!

The site is like an entire mile long.

We are building a lumber mill.

Sometimes I seriously stop and think, how in the hell is this my life now?

Anyway…

I’ve been living up the single life.

I took myself to see the Broadway musical Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat, and it was phenomenal.

I’ve been going to two or three AA meetings and church every week in AR.

I even have my first official friend! His name is Luke. He’s a gay guy I met in AA, and we’ve gone to the Museum of Fine Arts together and hit up meetings.

I’ve gone on some dates too…

But nothing to talk about yet.

Honestly, I’m really enjoying just being me right now.

I’m learning how to enjoy my own company, focus on my career, and let life unfold instead of trying to force it.

And apparently part of this new adventure is figuring out who I am when I’m not surviving some kind of crisis.

Turns out…

I kinda like her.

I love and miss you all.

PLEASE WRITE ME BACK! Seriously. Your messages help me more than you probably realize.

I’m doing amazing, but I still get lonely once in a while. Hearing from y’all lifts my spirits and reminds me that some of the people who understand this journey the most are still right there.

I can’t wait until every one of you gets to walk into your own place, look around, and say:

Mine.

Until then, I’m out here rooting for you.

XOXO.

posts.title: I’m Not Ready to Write This
posts.excerpt:
I’m not ready to write this.

But I’m writing it anyway.
posts.content:
1/21/26

I’m not ready to write this first post.

At least, not the one people might expect. I know there’s plenty to say, but that would mean taking apart the compartments I’ve built so carefully.

What if they’re the only reason I function, survive, and keep moving forward without falling apart? Oh God, what if I’m nothing without them?

Emotional detachment and dissociation have been my favorite coping mechanisms for a long time. I’m practically an expert now.

I just don’t know if I’m ready to let that go.

So this is me showing up anyway. Not with answers. Not with a breakthrough. Just being honest about where I’m starting. I’m learning to sit with discomfort instead of filing it away for later. I’m getting there.

I’m not ready to write this.
But I’m writing it anyway.

posts.title: The Day I Walked Away
posts.excerpt:
Sometimes walking away isn’t giving up.

The day I walked away wasn’t the day I stopped loving someone.

It was the day I finally started loving myself.
posts.content:
Guys, I have a confession to make.

I stopped writing in real time like I promised, and you deserve to know why.

I wasn’t emotionally capable of writing this story as it unfolded.

Healing can be so messy. I began to shrink back inside myself without even realizing it was happening. Hayley saw it, but I didn’t listen.

Little by little, guilt and shame found the tiny cracks that still existed in my soul and crept back in. Until suddenly, I was watching my life from the outside in. Once again.

I didn’t want anyone to know. Not because I was pretending everything was okay. Because I honestly wasn’t sure if it was.

I went to work every day. I smiled at the right times. I kept checking all the right boxes.

I stayed clean and sober, but another solution quietly found its way back into my life in a desperate need for validation from a man. A need I genuinely thought I had buried in prison.

The man’s name is irrelevant. What he taught me isn’t.

Here’s my disclaimer. Everything he ever told me might have been true, but truth is often subjective, isn’t it? That part isn’t what’s important though.

Because this story isn’t really about him. It’s about what healing in real time looks like. 

The first time he became upset with me, his reaction triggered trauma I thought I’d left behind.

His voice was no longer just his but blurred together with every toxic man in my past who ever hurt me, beat me, degraded me.

My father. My husband. Other past relationships.

I could no longer tell the difference.

I was no longer reacting to the man standing in front of me anymore but to every man who had ever made me believe I wasn’t enough.

That wasn’t fair to him, but it also wasn’t fair to me.

Every joke he made, I took to heart and my newfound confidence waned.

Every disappearance became another abandonment.

Every suggestion sounded like control.

It was like he knew exactly how to break me. Little by little, I crawled back into the shell I had spent years trying to escape. He isolated me or I isolated myself, especially from Hayley. I didn’t want anyone to know.

At one point, I almost convinced myself to stay.

I heard my father saying I should be grateful for less than I deserved.

“If a successful man is willing to take you on after everything you’ve done, you should be grateful.”

“Don’t mess this up. What value do you really bring to the relationship anyway?”

Those voices had been quiet for a while. Now they were screaming again. 

I began believing the disrespect, the criticism, the control were what I deserved. I convinced myself it was still better than my best day using.

He once told me I would always have a home with him. I think he knew exactly what that word meant to me.

Home.

After addiction.

After prison.

After motels.

After couches.

Even storage units.

Home was the one thing I wanted more than anything else in the world. And I clung to that word long after I should have let go.

We always knew he would eventually leave Florida. He wanted to find a way around all the red tape in my life so I could join him. On paper, it sounded like hope.

Inside, I was falling apart.  In the end, I was praying for him to leave while begging him to stay. I needed him to leave like I needed breath in my lungs, but my heart was still stuck in his hand.

When he went home, we were still making plans for my arrival. He apologized for his behavior. He promised things would be different when I got “home”. He said he had only acted the way he did because he was scared to lose me.

Sound familiar?

Finally, I prayed hard enough and listened long enough to hear God whisper, “I am strong, and I am worthy.”

So I was the one who walked away. And I never looked back.

Walking away hurt, but it was also the most liberating experience of my life. 

I don’t hate him. I don’t resent him. I genuinely hope he continues to succeed.

I hope his business thrives. I hope he finds peace. I hope he finds love.

I genuinely hope he finds the woman who makes him truly happy.

It just isn’t me.

I was fighting a war he could never fully understand. Not against him. Against every voice that convinced me I had to earn love by accepting less than I deserved.

Walking away hurt. It left new scars. But for the first time in my life, the scars didn’t remind me of what someone did to me. They reminded me of what I finally did for myself.

I didn’t learn how to never get hurt again. I learned that loving myself has to come before loving anyone else.

And maybe that’s what healing in real time really is. Not avoiding pain. Not pretending old wounds don’t reopen.

It’s recognizing when they do and choosing yourself anyway. 

Choosing to never disappear again.

posts.title: Me, According to Google
posts.excerpt:
What if I was always judged by my worst day?

What if I wasn’t?
posts.content:
The Woman Behind the Headline

If I was always judged by my worst day, I’d never be given a chance.

This was the moment every person with a sordid past and untold secrets dreads.

The moment you realize your worst day has arrived before you have.

Mine showed up on a Saturday morning in late January.

I had barely sat down at work when our HR Director walked into the office.

“Is there anything you want to tell me about your background?”

I froze. My stomach dropped. Dread and fear consumed me, and I had to remind myself to breathe.

Not because I had lied. Not because I had hidden my past. I hadn’t.

When I filled out my application, I checked the box.

Yes. I have a felony.

No one asked me about it. Not during the interview. Not after I was hired. Not once.

Until that Saturday morning.

The one thing I had feared the most since the day I walked out of prison was finally happening.

I had finally built a life I was beginning to love. A future I was excited about.

And in one conversation, I was convinced I was about to lose it all.

My mind was racing.

Did someone Google me? Did they find the article?

Does she know the final verdict or just the media’s version of my story?

Has she already judged me?

Has the decision about my future already been made for me again?

Suddenly, I wasn’t sitting in that office anymore. I was right back in prison. Scared to leave because I was terrified I’d fail.

The crazy part is that twenty-four hours earlier, I had told my boss everything.

Not because he asked. Not because I had to. Just because I was tired of carrying it around. So thankfully, he already knew.

Prison. Probation. Recovery. The addiction. The mistakes. All of it.

I held nothing back.

I thought I was finally taking control of my story.

I had no idea someone else was about to try to tell it for me.

Turns out the woman from the yellow house still had me in her sights and had decided to introduce me to my new employer.

Not by my work ethic.

Not by my professionalism.

Not by the woman I was becoming.

By my mugshot.

My news article had been emailed throughout the company.

The HR Director.

The company president.

My boss.

Members of my boss’s family.

Probably more people than I will ever know.

Anyone and everyone this person thought should know who I “really” was.

So there I was…

Where so many people leaving prison or rebuilding their lives eventually find themselves.

Holding my breath.

Panicking.

Waiting to find out whether my past had just stolen my future.

Thankfully…

It didn’t.

But that isn’t really why I tell this story.

I’m telling it because that morning taught me something I hope every person rebuilding their life hears loud and clear.

People can meet you in one of two ways.

They can meet your worst mistake.

Or they can meet the person you’ve become.

I couldn’t stop someone from finding my mugshot or the news article.

But I had already done something far more important.

I had told my story first.

And I’m not even talking about the conversation I had with my boss the day before.

I’m talking about my work ethic.

My professionalism.

My drive.

The way I showed up every single day.

I had gone above and beyond to prove my value long before anyone found my past.

So when the article finally showed up…

It wasn’t introducing me.

It was introducing someone I used to be.

That doesn’t mean it didn’t hurt.

It did.

That doesn’t mean shame didn’t come rushing back.

It did.

That doesn’t mean I wasn’t terrified.

I absolutely was.

For a few minutes, I had myself convinced one Google search was about to erase every blessing that had happened since prison.

But it didn’t.

Because God and recovery had already done what the headline never could.

They changed the person behind it.

The article hadn’t become untrue.

It had simply become incomplete.

My mugshot will probably outlive me.

The internet has a long-ass memory.

That woman in the article will always be part of my story.

She just doesn’t get to tell it anymore.

When my mugshot walked into that office that Saturday morning…

For the first time in my life…

It was no longer the loudest voice in the room.

The woman I had become sang louder.

posts.title: Look at God Y’all
posts.excerpt:
Seven months ago, I was sitting in prison wondering what my future would look like.

Today, I’m packing for Arkansas, getting the keys to my OWN place, sponsoring other women, and helping my son fix his car.

Look at God, y’all.
posts.content:
6/22/26

Sorry it has been a minute since my last update. I had to order a new debit card, and it is STILL not here.

Good news though.

I bought an alternator, and my son got his car running again.

Thank God!!! I was losing it.

My oldest, Kylie, has been feeling better the past few weeks, so we have been talking every day. That makes me so happy.

My old boss tried to contact me from a restricted number (because he is still blocked), but I shut that down quickly. Go ME!

Did I tell you guys child support took $4,700 out of my savings account? Yep. I had been saving it as my emergency fund for traveling.

But… I owed it. So another 9th Step amend down.

Speaking of recovery… I have TWO sponsees now and spoke at a big AA meeting last night. Pretty freakin’ cool!

My company decided to put me on their biggest and most important project which is long-term.

And guess what??? I applied for an apartment just to see what would happen… AND I GOT APPROVED. You guys… I have been homeless, living in motels, couch surfing, or in prison for more than eight years.

Now I am about to have a place to call home again.

And for the first time in my life…

It is going to be ALL MINE. I wish my kids were going to be there with me. I wish that part of the story was different. But I am still incredibly grateful.

Here’s to new adventures!

Sometimes I still cannot believe this is my life.

Only seven months ago, I was sitting in prison wondering what would happen when I got out.

Today…

I am packing for Arkansas.

Helping my son fix his car.

Sponsoring other women.

Getting the keys to my very own apartment.

And preparing for a future I wasn’t sure I would ever get to have.

Look at God, y’all.

I love you guys.

posts.title: Rainbows, Butterflies, & Reality
posts.excerpt:
I absolutely refuse to live in self-pity again.

So I’m just going to keep suiting up, showing up, and trusting that one day my children will know the woman I’ve become.
posts.content:
5/24/26 <-THIS IS THE DATE I ACTUALLY WROTE THIS LETTER!

Hello, hello!

Sorry it has been a few weeks.

Overall, things are going really well. Some days it probably sounds like my life is all rainbows and butterflies.

But reality still has a way of showing up.

The difference today is that I don’t completely melt down when things don’t go my way anymore. I take a deep breath, pray, and walk through the different possibilities instead.

The first big thing that happened was that I finally cut ties with my old boss completely. His ex called my probation officer AGAIN. No friendship is worth risking my freedom. I blocked him completely and haven’t spoken to him since. My officer wants me to file a no stalking order against her.

I am also no longer seeing the guy I kept mentioning. The one I lived with for a month.

Am I a little sad? Yes. 

But mostly… I have my calm, boring life back. And it is peaceful.

I still fight loneliness sometimes. I realized I was using the attention of men, texting and going on a few dates, as a distraction. It wasn’t leading me anywhere healthy.

So this weekend, I went back to something I knew filled my cup.

Church. Dinner. AA Meeting. Back to my Saturdays with Hayley. I forgot how much I needed that.

Now for the hard part. I still haven’t seen my children. My sister and I are doing amazing and slowly rebuilding our relationship, but the kids still aren’t showing any signs of being ready for one with me.

My son finally picked up the car I gave him. I paid for the tag and registration, and yesterday he drove it home.

Then almost the worst possible thing happened.

The car (which never gave me one single issue) broke down halfway to his house after shaking and smoking. I was distraught. I prayed the situation would bring us together, but it has not. He still isn’t comfortable seeing or talking to me.

We communicate through my sister about the car, which is still progress. On Mother’s Day, he asked her to tell me how grateful he was that I paid for the tag and registration. Hearing that meant more than he probably realizes.

My friend is going to look at the car after work to see if it can be fixed or at least diagnosed. I paid for the tow home, and I will do whatever I can to help. I just want my son to know that if he needs me, I will show up.

I just don’t understand why the one area of my life that matters more than anything else always seems to be the hardest. Don’t get me wrong. I am incredibly grateful for my job, my recovery, my car, and the friendships God has given me.

But my children…

They are my heart.

After a good cry and a whole lot of praying, I decided all I can do is keep moving forward and stay grateful for the blessings I have today. I absolutely refuse to live in self-pity again.

It looks like I will be assigned my first travel assignment around the second week of June. I am nervous and excited. Mostly, overwhelmed. But what an incredible opportunity for a fresh start with people who know my past and still believe in me.

So…

Let’s go.

Oh! Did I tell you I got asked to be on another podcast? This one is for the coding program I completed in prison. They highlight success stories, and they actually asked me to be one of them. My episode airs June 5. What an honor.

I think that’s about it for now. Please pray that my son’s car can be fixed without costing too much. But even more than that… Please pray for my relationship with my children.

I love you all.

posts.title: The Keys were the Prize for the Prep
posts.excerpt: I honestly thought they were going to change their mind and ask for the keys back. Turns out the hardest part wasn’t buying the car… it was becoming the person ready to drive it.
posts.content:
5/2/26 <-***Date I wrote this blog***

I am so excited to tell you what I did last Sunday.

Y’all are the first people I thought of and wanted to tell.

Since I am going to be traveling for work, I needed a newer, more reliable car. My heart was set on a Camry.

I looked at a few cars by owner, and then on a whim, I stopped at a dealership. I looked at three cars and went home to sleep on it.

The next day, I walked back into the dealership and said,

“I want the 2020 Toyota Camry with 26K miles.”

And within three hours… I was driving away with the keys!!! I put a good down payment down to keep my monthly payments lower. I promise I am still trying to make responsible decisions over here. 😂

Honestly, the whole time I was sitting there, I kept expecting someone from the dealership to walk into the lobby laughing and tell me to leave.

The credit application asked for three years of address history. So…

I listed my current address. Then the prisons. I am working an honest program today, so… LMAO.

I still couldn’t believe they handed me the keys.

Thursday, I got my old car detailed and signed the title over to my son. My sister picked it up for him.

I continue to pray about my relationship with my children. My sister and I are really close now.

I got my first paycheck with my big girl salary, so that was nice. Obviously, I have done my budget over and over and over again because… well… it’s me. I had to make sure I was okay. I definitely am. I can save 25% of my monthly income and still live comfortably. My youngest daughter turns sixteen next year, so I guess I better start saving for another car now!

God is so good. The moment I stop trying to force things and actually let go and let God, blessings shower me. It is crazy.

But I want you guys to know something important…

I did a lot of preparation in prison too. So start now. The most important thing I did was learn how to be happy on my own. I spent most of my time by myself, whether that was reading my Bible, playing a game, writing, or making those memory books for my kids I loved to show off. I even finished an entire self-help book in there just because it could possibly help. I was willing to try anything.

I also took my mental health seriously and did my best to address my codependency because drugs were only one issue of many. There were so many other things I had to face.

I am nowhere near perfect. I was literally just crying because my dude pissed me off. Still human over here.

But at the end of the day, I have a life I never imagined having less than six months after walking out.

And I need you to hear this:

You can have it too.

Love you.

posts.title: Look What God Did
posts.excerpt:
Five months ago, I was sitting in prison.

Today, I have a stable job, a savings account, a new car on the way, and more opportunities than I know what to do with.

God is still in the miracle business.
posts.content:
4/19/26 <-DATE WRITTEN

Hi there!

Sorry it’s been so long! I have so much great news to share with you all. I honestly cannot believe all of the blessings God keeps putting in my life. Where do I even start?

I got into the coding boot camp that pays you to go to school! I thought 40 people were selected for each cohort, but I was actually 1 of only 10 people chosen. The instructor even showed my website submission as an example of what he was looking for. I was so honored.

At the same time, my temporary job offered me a full-time traveling position. Probation approved it, but I will have to renew my travel pass every 30 days. It will be inconvenient, but it is worth it. I am also NOT ready to completely transfer my probation to another state until I am more stable and established on my own.

After a lot of prayer and thought, I decided to turn down the boot camp and accept the job. The boot camp no longer guarantees job placement, and I will actually be making more money than I would have starting out in a coding career.

I want all of you to understand what is possible. Five months ago, I was sitting where you are. Today, I am making 6-figures if you add in per diem and vehicle allowances!

I am giving my son my car for his 18th birthday because I am buying a new one that will be reliable for all of my travel. I have a savings account. I have a stable job. Life is good.

I still go to my meetings, and I was asked to speak at an AA meeting this Wednesday. It is a big meeting, so I am nervous, but I am excited.

I went to church today and had lunch with a couple of girlfriends. Those simple moments mean more to me than I can explain.

About the guy I am with. Listen, I care about him a lot, but for the first time in my life, I am not rushing anything.

He has offered me a home, his extra vehicle, financial stability, and an easier path, but I need to prove to myself that I can build my own life first.

I love you all and miss you!

Love,
Amy

posts.title: BUT WAIT. THERE’S MORE.
posts.excerpt:
Lifetime movie drama.
BUT WAIT.
A national coding interview.
BUT WAIT.
A possible move across the country.
BUT WAIT.
A dream job offer.
THERE’S MORE!
posts.content:
**3/28/26** ACTUAL DATE WRITTEN

Hi guys!

I love you all. Your messages make me smile and literally make me laugh out loud sometimes.

I am doing really well. Not everything is perfect at all. I will give you the terrifying Lifetime movie drama first, and then I will get to all the good stuff. The key is, as long as I stay clean, I know I will keep winning.

DRAMA:

I don’t even know how much I have told you, but my life has turned into a Lifetime movie. There has been so much drama involving my old boss’s ex or whatever she is that it honestly does not even feel real. He now has a no-stalking order in place, and I am doing everything I can to focus on peace and moving forward.

The kicker was when his ex called my probation officer and made a false report about guns being where I lived that led to me being handcuffed and the house I was staying being searched. They later apologized and explained that they were following protocol, but I will never forget the feeling of sitting there in handcuffs knowing I had done nothing wrong terrified of going back to prison for ten years.

I have moved again (yes, I know). This makes the fourth place I have lived since getting out of prison, but honestly, this one has been my favorite so far. I have my own room in a beautiful home right on the water, and I have met some truly good people who have reminded me how much kindness still exists in the world.

GOOD NEWS:

I got a second interview for the Next Chapter Coding Boot Camp!!! I’ll send you a screenshot of the home page for the website I submitted!!!

I am excited. I am terrified. I am trying not to get my hopes up too much.

And somehow, because my life apparently needed another major decision to make, I have even more choices.

The guy I am seeing has offered for me to come live with him rent free while I complete the coding boot camp and focus on my writing. The craziest part? I told my mom and sister expecting them to tell me I was completely out of my mind and that they would never support it because it was way too soon.

Instead, they said, “What’s the worst that happens? It doesn’t work out and you tried.”

They also pointed out that he had many qualities I had never experienced in past relationships. He was successful, stable, and had never struggled with addiction.

BUT WAIT. There is more 😂.

My current job also offered me a full-time traveling Onboarding Specialist /Project Manager Assistant position. I am waiting for the official offer, but they know my entire past and have already told me they will help with anything probation requires for me to travel for work.

How cool is that?

I have so many incredible opportunities in front of me, and I am praying every day that I make the right decision.

I hope these letters bring you hope and make you smile. Keep writing me back. I love and miss all of you.

Love,

Amy

posts.title: Blessings, Boundaries, and Bad Decisions
posts.excerpt:
Good things kept coming through the storms.

A driver’s license. A car. Recovery. A job I loved. Feelings I wasn’t supposed to have.

What could possibly go wrong? 😂
posts.content:
**2/1/26** ACTUAL DATE WRITTEN

*A quick reminder:** Just because I am posting this today does not mean I wrote it today.

These letters were written in real time and are being shared later. I am allowing you to read my thoughts exactly as they existed before I knew how the next chapter would unfold……………………..

Hi guys!

Life has been INSANE. I don’t even have time to update you on everything, but I am going to try.

I only have a few stamps, so I cannot send prepaid replies. I’m sorry. I am having to pick and choose who I can send this to — basically all of you who actually write me back regularly!!!

I got my driver’s license back on Thursday and bought a cheap car this weekend!!! Next week, I will get the tag, title, and insurance and be back on the road.

The funniest thing is I don’t even really need the car right now. My roommate Hayley and my boss both WANT to drive me around.

I feel so loved. Honestly, I think that is the ultimate compliment. They both just want to keep every minute they can get with me.

Speaking of my boss…

I don’t even know where to start. Everyone was accusing us of having a relationship. We were always professional. I mean, we flirted, but nothing else had happened.

Then the drama started. You guys know I HATE drama. Like, truly hate it. But I also couldn’t quit my job.

Ironically, the more people and circumstances seemed to be trying to pull us apart, the more we were pushed toward each other.

By the way, he knows EVERYTHING now.

My past.

Prison.

Probation.

All of it.

He has been very protective of me, and I greatly appreciate that.

I have done really well at work and have proved not only my ability to do everything asked of me and more, but also my ability to separate work and personal life completely.

If my sister does not let me have at least a phone call with the kids soon, I am thinking of filing a motion. I just need to be emotionally ready for whatever that brings and make sure whatever happens is what is best for them.

I am starting my 8th Step now. I still go to four or five meetings every week.

I am also chairing my home group meeting on Tuesdays in March, so I will lead the meeting and pick the speakers.

Good things keep coming through the storms.

Love you.

posts.title: Somehow, This Is My Life Now
posts.excerpt:
I still catch myself expecting to wake up in a prison bunk.

Instead, I wake up to work, recovery, friendships, new opportunities, and entirely too many things to be grateful for.

Somehow, this is my life now.
posts.content:
1/15/26 <- Date Sent

My goal is to write to you every other week.

I got my first 60-hour check. My boss signed a letter to child support saying I need my license for work, so I submitted that. I am putting half down on a used car tomorrow and the other half on January 30. Then I can get insurance and registration the first week of February. I am so excited.

The crazy thing is that my friend who takes me to work every day and picks me up four or five days a week AND even my boss said they are kind of sad about me getting a car and not spending as much time with them.

What a great compliment!

So much happens out here. I am trying to think of what I want to tell you. This could go on past the 20,000-character limit.

Trust me.

I work 6:45AM to 5:30PM Monday through Saturday. I have a lot to do now, but it still doesn’t seem much like work.

My boss and I have become really good friends. He even took me to the doctor today. I had to have surgery on my face to get a terribly large cyst removed. He stayed with me and everything. I only needed one stitch.

Oh, and he even took me to see the car I am buying last week.

I still talk to Tesla Guy sometimes. He is in California for a conference for work.

He said he wanted to talk about us and admitted he wanted more, but I told him I didn’t have more to give right now. We did go to lunch before he went out of town though.

I am barely two months out of prison, but honestly, he is the type of person I should probably be looking at long-term. He is stable, trustworthy, has several years clean, a great job, and somehow manages to avoid drama.

I need to find my own way before I start worrying about relationships and titles.

At least that is what I keep telling myself.

I still go to four or five meetings a week.

I am doing step work with my sponsor tomorrow night.

I am the treasurer for the Oxford House I live in and the reentry chair for my chapter. Oxford House is definitely the place to be if you are serious about recovery and looking at transitional housing.

One of the things I look forward to most every week is Saturday with Hayley. We go to church, then dinner, then a meeting. It has become our little routine, and we both look forward to it so much.

Oh, and guess what?

My sponsor and another guy from recovery do a podcast called Rated R for Recovery on Tuesday nights at 6PM. I am going to be the guest speaker on March 10! Crazy, right? I wish I could get it to you guys. Maybe I could talk to the guy who runs it about getting it into prisons. That would be so cool.

Sometimes I still catch myself thinking I am going back to my bunk after all this.

Then I remember I have work in the morning, bills to pay, a podcast to prepare for, and entirely too many men giving me things to overthink.

Life is weird.

But in a good way.

I am so tired.

Long day.

Going to bed.

Love you.

posts.excerpt: I swear my life is boring. Unfortunately, the evidence continues to suggest otherwise.
posts.content:
**1/8/26** Date Written

Listen guys, I really do lead a boring life.

It’s just that prison is so boring, with such limited options, that my life out here probably seems crazy by comparison.

I’m trying to remember where my last update stopped. I know I had just started my new job.

It is still going great. Honestly, it doesn’t even feel like work because we have so much fun. There are pros and cons to that though.

Trust me.

My ridiculously attractive boss and I have this smart-ass banter that keeps us laughing all day. He’s joked about taking me to the Keys.

Little does he know, I can’t even cross the county line, so now, just in case he is serious, I am trying to figure out why I’m mysteriously booked solid for the next three months until this project is over and he goes back home, halfway across the country.

On a more practical note, I’m getting about sixty hours a week, so my paychecks are amazing.

If everything goes according to plan, I should have a cheap car by the end of the month. How cool is that?

Right now, one of my roommates, Hayley, takes me to work every day and picks me up afterward. Even before she started her new job, she was doing it for me, and trust me, it is not a short drive.

How blessed can one person be? I am so grateful for the friendships I’ve already built out here. It amazes me how many people have shown up for me when I needed them most.

For those of you who were in our Persevere coding class…

Congratulations!!! I am waiting to hear how everything went. They said they were going to read my message to the class and give you copies because there wasn’t enough time to get my video approved.

It’s funny.

A few months ago, I was sitting where you are.

Today I’m working sixty hours a week, trying to buy a car, getting rides from my roommate, and figuring out how to explain to my ridiculously attractive boss why I can’t leave the county.

Life is weird.

But in the best possible way.

posts.title: What the Hell Did I Walk Into?
posts.excerpt:
A cute guy. A lake house. A screaming girlfriend. A panic-induced Lyft ride.

What could possibly go wrong? Everyone loves a good Lifetime movie….
posts.content:
Mid-January 2026

There are moments in life when you realize you have made a series of questionable decisions.

For example:

Accepting an invitation to spend the afternoon with your ridiculously attractive boss and others from work.

Driving nearly an hour into the middle of nowhere.

Ending up at a bright yellow house on a lake with a man whose aura practically screamed, “RUN!”

And then finding yourself trapped behind a locked sliding glass door while someone’s alleged long-time girlfriend screams obscenities at you through the screen.

That was my Saturday.

And somehow…

That isn’t even the craziest part……

It’s January 17, 2026. Two months and three days out of a five-year prison sentence.

My boss is constantly trying to give me rides.

Sometimes it’s to a “doctor’s appointment” that is actually probation. Other times it’s the behavioral health center. He also regularly offers to drive me home, but I am absolutely not ready to explain why I live in a halfway house.

At all.

I don’t know what I was thinking, but on this particular Saturday, I decided to accept an invitation to his house to “cheer him on” while he changed the oil in his motorcycle. The superintendent and his room mates from work were coming too, so why not?

To be fair, I really did want a ride on the back of the motorcycle.

The entire drive there, I was a nervous wreck.

What am I doing?

And underneath all of that was another thought:

Saturday is Hayley and my night.

Church. Dinner. A meeting.

Our routine.

I shouldn’t be canceling on her for a man.

That should have been my first clue to stay home.

Second clue was I had no intention of staying the night, and they were already talking about drinking. That meant there was absolutely no way I was letting him take me home afterward.

Obvious red flag.

A reasonable person would have changed their mind right then.

I did not.

Everything about this man made me want to throw caution to the wind and ignore every bit of common sense I had worked so hard to develop.

So naturally, I got in the truck.

The drive felt… weird.

He kept calling the superintendent to make sure he was coming.

Then he called him again.

And again.

Maybe he was having second thoughts.

Maybe I was too.

We stopped for random things along the way, including mint leaves for mojitos. Meanwhile, he still had no clue I didn’t drink.

The drive felt like forever.

At some point, we were deep in the town where he was staying, and he suddenly announced that he didn’t recognize where we were.

We had been driving down the same road for at least ten minutes.

How was he just now noticing?

He turned on GPS.

We were still fifteen minutes away and somehow heading in the wrong direction.

What the hell was happening?

We finally pulled into the driveway.

The house was bright yellow.

Not pale yellow. Not beige pretending to be yellow.

Bright yellow.

It was gorgeous inside and exactly the kind of place I would have imagined for him.

He disappeared into the kitchen while I wandered around taking everything in. Floor-to-ceiling sliders stretched across the back of the house, opening to a pool, hot tub, lake, and one of the prettiest sunsets I had seen in a while.

For a moment, I thought maybe I had been overthinking everything.

I kicked off my shoes, settled into a lounge chair, and enjoyed the fresh air.

Then the superintendent arrived.

They asked what I wanted to drink.

“I’m good,” I said.

They laughed.

My boss yelled, “What? Have you been sober for five years or something?”

I laughed nervously.

“Something like that.”

And suddenly… Everything felt weird.

The house had a terrible aura.

I know that sounds ridiculous, but it’s the only way I can describe it.

The beauty of the place had sucked me in at first. Now I felt a sense of impending doom I couldn’t explain.

I couldn’t relax.

I couldn’t make conversation.

Then I saw movement at the screen door.

A woman.

Thankfully, the door was locked.

As I watched her standing there, pieces of the day started falling into place.

The phone calls he took in private all day.

Him disappearing around 2PM without telling me.

That may not sound strange, but trust me, it was.

He took me everywhere with him.

Always.

Then there was the strange detour.

The nervous energy.

The way he kept checking to make sure everyone else was coming.

Standing there, staring at a woman on the other side of that screen door, I realized that maybe this wasn’t as unexpected as he wanted me to believe.

She looked a little unhinged.

With a mix of anger and disgust, she pointed at me and said,

“So you’re Amy.”

Then she looked at my boss.

“I thought nothing was going on.”

Then she looked back at me.

“Amy, I’m his long-time girlfriend. Are you sleeping with him?”

Through a combination of accusations, profanity, and details I never asked for, I pieced together that she believed they were still together and had been told to leave the yellow house earlier that day because someone from corporate was flying in early that night.

Apparently, my presence was proof that she had been lied to.

I don’t remember exactly what she said after that.

I just remember the volume and the anger.

I wanted absolutely no part of whatever this was.

Inside, I was completely panicking.

I don’t do drama.

More importantly, I can’t do drama.

If the police got called or things escalated in any way, I wasn’t just dealing with an awkward evening.

I was dealing with a possible probation violation and ten years back in prison.

Without saying a word, I picked up my shoes, walked back into the house, and slid the glass door shut behind me.

Then I called Hayley completely terrified.

The second she answered, I started talking way too fast.

“I’m so sorry, but you have to come get me. You have to come get me right now.”

She immediately told me to breathe and asked what was wrong.

She told me she would come get me, but gently reminded me that I was almost an hour away.

Then she said something that somehow hadn’t even crossed my mind.

“If you need to leave right now, call a Lyft.”

I hadn’t even thought of that.

By now, everyone was back inside, and the sliding glass doors were locked.

The woman had moved to the front door and was still screaming obscenities.

I walked over to my boss.

“Get me a Lyft right now. I’m leaving.”

He looked disappointed.

Then he told me he didn’t have the app and would have to download it.

I waved him off.

“I don’t have time for that. You can give me the money at work on Monday.”

For a moment, his face lit up.

“So I get to see you Monday? You’re not quitting?”

I shook my head.

“No. I’m not quitting. I can’t. I need this job.”

Then I paused.

“You don’t understand how bad this situation is for me. If the police get called, I am screwed.”

He looked confused.

I wasn’t about to explain probation, halfway houses, and why a random domestic dispute in the middle of nowhere felt like my life was about to end.

Thankfully, there was a Lyft less than ten minutes away.

While I waited, the screaming continued.

Most of it was so vile and degrading that I don’t even want to repeat it.

But one comment got through.

The cyst on the side of my face.

My hair covered it, so most people never noticed it. But it had gotten huge, and I was incredibly self-conscious about it.

I had mentioned it to my boss before because I figured he’d eventually see it.

I just never showed it to him.

Now, standing outside the yellow house from hell, I was being told that he made fun of it behind my back.

My insecurity flared instantly, and I could feel my face turning beet red.

Ouch.

That one stung.

Of all the things she could have said, she somehow found the one thing that would get to me.

She got me with that one.

Eventually, the screaming stopped.

The superintendent had spent what felt like hours but must have only been around 20 minutes trying every tactic he could think of.

First, he explained that my boss didn’t want to see her.

Then he promised there would be a phone call later if she would just leave.

Somehow, it finally worked.

When my Lyft arrived, I asked the superintendent to walk me to the car.

I was not taking any chances.

I climbed into the back seat, shut the door, and let out a breath I felt like I’d been holding all night.

Then I called Hayley.

She was still heading to the 7PM meeting.

I was going to be late.

I was rattled.

But I was going.

I wasn’t going to let anything confuse my priorities.

I walk into the meeting late, but Hayley has a seat saved with a huge bottle of water and a peanut butter Snickers waiting for me.

My heart melts with gratitude.

I love this woman.

I am not okay.

But I will be.

I always am.

That’s how I roll.

posts.title: How Many People Have You Killed?
posts.excerpt:
The question wasn’t the hardest part.

The hardest part was realizing how quickly people decide who you are after hearing where you’ve been.
posts.content:
1/20/26

“How many people have you killed?” my boss asked.

I froze.

Let me back up.

My boss and I have a pretty smart-ass banter. We were joking earlier about the fact that I don’t cook. At all. I hate it. We laughed. Conversation moved on.

Later, I was working on daily reports and completely forgot what we’d been talking about.

So when, from the other room, he casually asked, “So… how many people have you killed?” my body reacted before my brain could catch up. My stomach dropped. My mind raced. Terror, anxiety, and embarrassment all showed up at once.

I didn’t answer. I didn’t move. I just froze.

Thankfully, I’ve learned not to react immediately when I’m caught off guard. I took a deep breath and tried to figure out what was actually happening.

Of course, my first thought was, Did he Google me?
And right on the heels of that, If he had, would he really ask me like that? From the other room?

No. He wouldn’t.

I knew I was missing something, so as casually as I could manage, I asked, “What do you mean?”

He walked back into the office we’re currently sharing and said, “With your cooking. How many?”

The relief was instant. I tried not to let it show as I laughed and said, “How can I kill anyone with my cooking if I literally never cook?”

“Good point,” he said.

Then we went back to work. Conversation over.

Crisis averted.
For now.

posts.title: Dear Prison Pals — I’m Building Something New
posts.excerpt:
New job. New blog. Same fear I might lose it all.
But this time, I’m choosing to show up anyway.
posts.content:
12/28/26 <-DATE WRITTEN

Okay… I’m back. I meant to send my last update a week ago. My bad.

So I’ll just say it like this…
Things are still moving fast.

And now I have something new to share.

I’m starting a blog. I already bought the domain. I have the name and the tagline:

Cell to Self
Life, Rewritten in Real Time

And one of the series is going to be these letters… to YOU!!!

MY FIRST WEEK OF WORK went great… just not how I expected.

There was no electricity in the portable office, so I spent the entire week riding around in my boss’s truck. We visited the welders, talked through steel erection and fabrication, and I asked a million questions.

He shared a lot about his life. I answered mostly yes or no. He has no idea what my backstory is, so I kept it simple.

Also… I wish I had a picture to send you. This man is fine.

Like… rugged outdoors man meets Calvin Klein model. Perfect teeth. Blue eyes. Surfer hair. In good shape. VERY single. Made sure I knew that on day one.

And there I am, sitting next to him thinking:

Please don’t Google me. Please don’t Google me. Please don’t Google me.

He couldn’t get a flight home for Christmas, so I suggested he go to the Keys. He loved the idea.

Said he might come back married.

Honestly… I was just relieved he wouldn’t be bored in a town where he knows no one and decide to Google me.

I still have this fear that I’m going to show up to work one day and be asked to leave.

But the truth is… I think eventually, I’ll tell him.

Not everything. But enough.

Because we actually get along really well. The banter is there. The sarcasm. The quick wit. It’s easy.

And from what he’s shared about his own past… I don’t think he would judge me the way I’m afraid of.

I just want to prove my value first.

Before I start saying things like:
“I need child support taken out of my check.”
“I need a letter to get my driver’s license back.”
“Oh, and by the way… I’m on probation.”

QUICK LIFE UPDATE…

I am seeing the Tesla guy again, with my sponsor’s guidance.

We’ve hung out 5 or 6 times. The fourth time, I finally let him kiss me.

That’s it.

I am moving slow. As slow as possible.

He has four years clean, a good job, and he’s very self-aware.

So… we’ll see.

AND FINALLY…

I went to the beach for the first time since I’ve been out.

It was an AA meeting on Sanibel.

I put my feet in the sand. Let the water move over them. Sat in the sun reflecting off the ocean. Breathed. Listened.

And for a moment…

everything felt still.

WHAT ELSE?

I know I’m forgetting things.

But I’ll write more soon.

Love you.

posts.title: Dear Prison Pals — Things Are Moving Fast
posts.excerpt:
You may think these letters are helping you… but the truth is, you’re helping me just as much.
This week reminded me how much can change when you choose growth over old patterns.
posts.content:
12/21/26 <- When Written

This week has been crazy, and I need you to know something.

Your messages are helping keep me strong.

I met some of the most amazing people and best friends in there. You may think my messages are helping you, but yours are helping me so much more than you know. Even when I don’t have prepaid replies to send, you’re still showing up. You make me feel loved when I’m overwhelmed. You put a smile on my face even out here.

Because of that—and because things moved fast the last few days—I already have another update.

I didn’t move forward with the Tesla guy… again.

It honestly wasn’t about him. It was me. I saw something in myself I’ve never really stopped long enough to notice before—emotional immaturity. I rush. I attach. I become co-dependent. And for the first time in my life, I chose to stop.

I’m actually proud of that.

I just finished my 4th and 5th steps with my sponsor, and I feel more free than I have in a long time. I let go of a lot of trauma. I may try dating again in the new year… but for now, I’m choosing growth.

I turned in my onboarding paperwork for my new job.

I checked “yes” on the felony question.
I consented to the background check.
And then… I waited.

No one has said anything yet.

I have my company laptop. My email is set up. I start on site at 6AM. I’m still bracing myself for the moment it might come up, but for now, I’m choosing to be excited for the opportunity in front of me.

I will actually be in full PPE tomorrow, stepping into where the construction is happening for the first time. I’ll try to get a picture with my hard hat!

I had a rough afternoon recently.

My old boss from the ministry is getting worse. His dementia. He called me, accusing me of things that weren’t real like stealing a piece of paper, making threats like sending me back to prison. It was scary and made no sense.

I called my mom. We reached out to people who might be able to help him, but I had to make a hard decision—I cut ties completely and blocked him.

After the call, I felt panic creeping in.

But I didn’t spiral.

I went to church anyway. I gave everything to God. Then I went to dinner and an AA meeting. And somewhere in the middle of that, your messages came through again—reminding me that I’m not alone.

I caught myself trying to take it all back from God later that day… and then I gave it back again.

That’s new for me.

I don’t wait until things are completely out of control anymore.

Growing up is hard.
But I am seriously adulting, guys.

The website I’m building is going really well.

My client loves the banner I designed. I created a mock homepage from a sketch he gave me, and he said it was exactly what he envisioned. Now I’m working on getting it live and building out pages for businesses to advertise.

It’s WordPress, but I’ve been able to write my own HTML and CSS into it, so it still feels like me.

Merry Christmas. Happy holidays. Sending my love.

posts.title: Dear Me,
posts.excerpt:
You don’t get to pretend you don’t remember what it took to get here.
This wasn’t handed to you—it was a rebuild. Piece by piece. Choice by choice.
And somehow, through all of it… you’re still becoming.
posts.content:
You made it out.

Not just out of a place—but out of a version of yourself that once felt permanent. And you don’t get to pretend you don’t remember what it took to get here.

The silence.
The waiting.

The time when your world was small, controlled, uncertain… and it broke you. Not in a clean way. Not in a pretty “before and after” way.

In a real way.

Now look at you… free and rebuilding.
Piece by piece.
Choice by choice.
Day by day when no one is watching.

That didn’t happen by accident. You fought for this version of your life.

You’re in the middle of becoming—and that middle is messy, quiet, and sometimes so lonely it echoes.

But look at what you’ve done.

You went from barely surviving… to solving problems.
From reacting first… to thinking things through.
From completely stuck… to rewriting your life in real time.

You’ve walked into rooms where you didn’t feel ready—and figured it out anyway.
You’ve led while still healing.
You’ve taken responsibility most people would run from.

Your life now isn’t built on luck.
It’s built on decisions.

The small ones.
The daily ones.
The ones no one sees.

Loving people… carefully now.
Protecting your peace… learning how.
Letting go… even when your hands don’t want to open.

And still—there’s a softness in you.

The part that writes.
The part that feels everything.
The part that still believes life can be rewritten.

Because it can.

You are proof.

So keep going.

Keep choosing growth over comfort.
Keep choosing honesty over avoidance.
Keep choosing yourself, even when it’s unfamiliar.

And when it gets heavy—

don’t look back at who you used to be.

Look at who you refused to stay.

— Me
